title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
authors: Yuhao Wu, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiajun Shi, Xinping Lei, Qingshui Gu, Yuxuan Zhang, Zexuan Wang, Chen He, Chen Huang, Maojia Song, Zhiyuan Zeng, Shaowen Wang, Jinkai Liu, Yunfeng Shi, Jiaheng Liu, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Ge Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang
lab: ByteDance Seed, Singapore University of Technology and Design, Georgia Institute of Technology, M-A-P, TokenWave.AI (core contributors Yuhao Wu, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiajun Shi)
date: 1 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far)

code.title: no code released
code.note: No code or data is linked yet. The paper says the reference seed, the audit script and the held-out task splits "will be released with the benchmark" (Appendix C), and that the audit artifacts are released (Ethics statement); the project page (ByteDance Seed and TokenWave) presents HarnessDev beside its two sibling benchmarks, Aspire and S3Gym, with interactive charts of the main results

takeaway: Moves evaluation from task performance to infrastructure construction: Creation (build an execution system from minimal components and sample cases) then Evolution (refine it from feedback), across six creator LLMs, four domains, five downstream benchmarks and 2,207 instances, scored on capability and execution-token cost; generated harnesses lag mature human references on code and search but match or beat them on writing and ML experimentation, while evolution gains are unstable, transfer poorly, and stay strongly dependent on which model executes the harness.
verdict: Believe the protocol and the warning about evolution: the score a creator can see moved the same way as the held-out score in only 34 of 64 version changes, and swapping the executing model can halve a harness's score. Treat the domain split as unproven: the references that generated harnesses lose to (code, search) ran newer, stronger models than any creator, while the ones they match ran the same or a similar model.

resources.t: Self-Developing Agents: From Half-Loop to Closed-Loop RSI
resources.by: ByteDance Seed and TokenWave, project page, 1 September 2026
resources.n: the authors' page for HarnessDev and its two sibling benchmarks (Aspire: can a model turn a vague goal into a target; S3Gym: can it learn from its own experience). Its HarnessDev panel charts the visible-against-held-out gains and the fixed-Gemini regressions.

resources.t: A 48-minute architecture playbook for building a reliable agent harness
resources.by: Stencil blog, filed on Topic: agentic-harnesses on 2026-09-07
resources.n: the human-written counterpart: state management, runtimes, control planes, tools and interfaces, with the thesis that unavoidable complexity belongs in a harness's core abstractions rather than in extensions.

resources.t: Evo-Bench: Can language models improve agent harness?
resources.n: the closest concurrent benchmark for the Evolution stage: evolver models improve a shared CodeAct seed with the runtime model fixed, scored on a disjoint multi-domain suite.

resources.t: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at harness optimization
resources.n: an optimizer gets a seed harness, graded feedback and a fixed budget; a trusted environment scores its nominated candidate on an inaccessible test partition. The paper calls it the closest concurrent work to Evolution.

resources.t: Harness updating is not harness benefit
resources.n: separates producing a useful harness update from an executor's ability to exploit it; the paper cites it as the motivation for splitting the creator from the executor.

resources.t: Meta-Harness: End-to-end optimization of model harnesses
resources.n: a coding-agent proposer that reads prior candidates, scores and traces before proposing the next harness: the method this benchmark measures in the wild.

resources.t: Inside the scaffold: a source-code taxonomy of coding agent architectures
resources.n: what mature coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands, SWE-agent) are made of; the background to the six modules E, T, C, S, L, V.
the source of the paper's opening example: the same GPT-5 weights at 35.2% in Terminus 2 and 49.6% in Codex CLI.

kb.n: the issue that covered this paper (Research and papers, 243 Hugging Face upvotes at the time) beside Repo-To-Skill and Terminal-Universe, and the ARC Prize Provider Adapter result and the harness playbook it is read against.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: a harness that versions its own prompts and skills across trajectories (Continual Harness); HarnessDev's Evolution results are the general check on whether such refinement compounds.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: trains a 27B model to emit a harness per task in a four-module protocol; HarnessDev asks untrained frontier models to build one in full.

kb.t: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a $15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
kb.n: the opposite pole: a human-written state machine that encodes domain procedure, on the same Terminal-Bench 2.1.

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: three weeks later: an annealed edit budget, a critic and a pruner, reporting +4.7 points out of distribution; the first answer to the overfitting HarnessDev measures.

kb.t: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
kb.n: the same loop pointed at cost instead of capability, where a cheap verifier exists (did it cost less and still pass?).

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: skills are one of the components a harness assembles; its finding that procedural anchors stabilise execution matches the verification gates that helped here.

kb.t: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
kb.n: the supply side: skills mined from repositories, from the same week.

kb.t: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
kb.n: the environments a harness-building model would need to practise in, from the same week.

topics.n: the harness-scaling strategies this benchmark measures, and the playbook filed there on 2026-09-07.
the open-source agent systems the paper draws its candidate references from (OpenHands, SWE-agent, gpt-researcher and others).
